root_cause.text: The v4l2_m2m_ctx_release() function only synchronizes the m2m job lifecycle (via TRANS_RUNNING flag) but does not wait for the workqueue handler (mtk_venc_worker) to complete, allowing the worker to access freed context memory after v4l2_m2m_job_finish() returns but before kfree(ctx) is called.
root_cause.evidence: The patch demonstrates that after v4l2_m2m_job_finish() signals job completion, the m2m framework returns from v4l2_m2m_ctx_release(), but mtk_venc_worker continues executing and accesses ctx->m2m_ctx, ctx->dev, and other ctx fields. The KASAN trace confirms use-after-free in mtk_venc_worker reading from freed memory (allocated in fops_vcodec_open, freed in fops_vcodec_release). The fix adds cancel_work_sync(&ctx->encode_work) before kfree(ctx) to synchronize the workqueue lifecycle, which was previously missing from the release path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending encode work before freeing context to prevent use-after-free when the workqueue handler accesses the context after v4l2_m2m_job_finish returns.
intent_record.what: Added a call to cancel_work_sync(&ctx->encode_work) in the fops_vcodec_release function, preceded by a detailed comment explaining the race condition being addressed.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that any pending work queued on the encode_work workqueue is cancelled and its handler completes before the context structure is freed. Without this, the mtk_venc_worker handler could access the context after it has been deallocated by kfree, causing a use-after-free memory error. The cancel_work_sync call blocks until the work item is no longer pending and any in-flight handler execution completes.
